A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIGTBench, OSM-Det, and social-media quantification study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding tables, figures, equations, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector benchmarking, social-media prevalence measurements, linguistic case studies, and engagement and author analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds generalization experiments, text-length analyses, and engagement results stratified by follower count.

M1.justification: OSM-Det remains LM-D using Longformer-base-4096 fine-tuned on AIGTBench. The detector architecture, classification procedure, training-data construction, and generation prompts are retained. The new pipeline illustration and disclosed hyperparameters do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation to unseen-generator outputs and external test scenarios. Appendix H and Tables A7–A8 add nine unseen-model polishing conditions and six external datasets, including Roleplay-English and InternVL-SA-1B-Caption. The original training datasets and Medium, Quora, and Reddit monitoring coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Both Table 2s evaluate the same 14 detectors, including ConDA, GPTZero, CheckGPT, and LM-D. The newly tested LLMs generate evaluation texts; they are not additional competing detectors.

E3.justification: New protocols polish 5,000 sampled HWTs while varying temperature/top-p from 0.1 to 1.0 and top-k from 1 to 200, evaluate unseen generators and external datasets, and stratify engagement by follower count. The stated vocabulary-selection source also changes from SM-D in v1 Appendix G.1 to AIGTBench in v2 Appendix I.1; unchanged words and plots do not establish that this analysis was rerun. The original 7:1:2 split remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds generation-parameter sensitivity tests, unseen-model/domain robustness tests, and performance analysis by text length (Figure 2, Figure A7, Appendix H). Table 3 additionally examines whether the engagement difference persists within follower groups. These substantially expand validation beyond v1; the existing linguistic case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same Mann–Whitney U tests with p < 0.05 for engagement. v2 introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or additional specified uncertainty-estimation procedures; the new experiments report point estimates.

E6.justification: The original Table 2 scores and social-media trend results remain unchanged. v2 adds platform-specific accuracies of 0.995/0.999/0.984 (Table A6), unseen-generator accuracies ranging from 0.925 to 0.999 (Table A8), and external-dataset accuracies from 0.943 to 0.999 (Table A7). Parameter and text-length curves and follower-group engagement means add substantial new results under additional conditions.

T1.justification: The AAR, FPR, and NTF definitions, including Equation 1, retain their mathematical substance. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: systematic social-media quantification, AIGTBench and OSM-Det, contrasting platform trends, and linguistic, engagement, and author differences. The added validation does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new generalization tests as supporting detector reliability and uses lower short-text accuracy to justify the existing length filter. Section 8 adds possible misclassification of pre-ChatGPT generators as a limitation. The interpretations of platform trends, engagement, and follower effects remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly discloses learning rate 1e-5, batch size 16, and AdamW; this does not establish changed training settings. Table 2 clarifies that F1 refers to the AI class. Appendix tables add dataset-domain metadata, and references identify sources for the new evaluation models and datasets.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new model/dataset evaluations and sharpens the distinction between interactive social-media content and formal news or academic writing. The principal related-work positioning remains. A citation regression also occurs: Appendix B's Longformer reference points to a translation paper in v2, whereas v1 cites the Longformer paper.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and metric explanations receive localized wording edits. New Appendices G–H precede the former Appendix G, now Appendix I. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained, so the revision does not constitute extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual evidence: it adds a pipeline diagram, parameter-sensitivity and text-length plots, and new result tables. The model-composition chart, FPR table, engagement plots, and Reddit vocabulary plot move into the appendix. Token-length histograms expand to all three splits, dataset tables gain domain columns, and the nine existing interpretation figures are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new transfer and sensitivity tests partially address v1's limited validation of detector reliability beyond its random-split benchmark. Follower-stratified engagement results and disclosed hyperparameters also strengthen the paper. However, missing sample counts for the external tests and the unexplained inclusion of sub-150-character texts despite Appendix E's filter limit the strength of this additional validation. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
